tasks.title: Author committed oracle tests/test_semantic_signals_wired.py asserting the taint_flow proof drives compute_confidence to CONFIRMED
acceptance_criteria: tests/test_semantic_signals_wired.py exists and is the file named in the verification_command.
The oracle runs the REAL stdlib AST verifier over inline source (hermetic — no network/subprocess/LLM/clock/randomness).
It asserts a real os.system sink on an exec-class finding yields a {'kind':'taint_flow','result':'proof'} signal from produce_semantic_signals.
It feeds that proof signal into ngv2.grounding_confidence_gate.compute_confidence and asserts the verdict is CONFIRMED.
It asserts clean source yields no proof signal (empty / no taint_flow proof).
The test passes against the correct module and fails against the declared mutant of ngv2.semantic_signals.

spec.objective: Provide the committed hermetic oracle that proves ngv2.semantic_signals is wired: a real os.system sink corroborating an execution-class finding produces a taint_flow structural proof that drives compute_confidence to CONFIRMED, while clean source produces no proof.
functional_requirements: Import produce_semantic_signals from ngv2.semantic_signals and compute_confidence from ngv2.grounding_confidence_gate; run entirely hermetically over inline source strings.

Assert that an exec-class finding (e.g. {'id':'command_injection','category':'command_injection','cwe':'CWE-78','evidence':['svc.py:3']}) over source containing a real os.system(...) sink yields at least one {'tool':'ast_verifier','kind':'taint_flow','result':'proof'} signal.
Assert that passing the produced proof signal(s) into compute_confidence returns a CONFIRMED verdict.
Assert that clean source (no exec sink) yields no taint_flow proof signal (empty list or no result=='proof').
spec.interfaces: Uses produce_semantic_signals(finding, source_code, language=None) and ngv2.grounding_confidence_gate.compute_confidence(signals). No new production interface introduced.
edge_cases: Source with os.system sink but a non-exec finding -> no taint_flow proof (negative control).
Tree-sitter wheels absent -> the test must still pass via the stdlib AST fallback path, exercising the lazy-import resilience.
non_goals: Do NOT modify ngv2/semantic_signals.py, the verifier modules, or grounding_confidence_gate.py.
Do NOT use network, subprocess, clock, randomness, or an LLM in the test.
spec.implementation_notes: Keep source strings inline so the run is hermetic and deterministic. The mutation_target is ngv2.semantic_signals: the test must fail if the proof-emission branch (rule in _EXEC_RULES and exec_finding) is broken/mutated, so assert specifically on kind=='taint_flow' and result=='proof' AND on the downstream CONFIRMED verdict.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Inline Python source with a real os.system(user_input) sink and a clean variant; exec-class finding dict and a non-exec finding dict. All assertions run against the real stdlib AST verifier — fully hermetic.

token_budget_ratio.note: This task IS the test; nearly all tokens are the oracle assertions, with minimal scaffolding.

tasks.title: Create ngv2/semantic_signals.py producing compute_confidence-shaped signals from the orphaned structural verifiers
acceptance_criteria: ngv2/semantic_signals.py exists with EXACTLY the content specified in the brief Deliverables (verbatim, byte-for-byte).
Module is importable as ngv2.semantic_signals even when optional tree-sitter grammar wheels are absent (verifier classes imported lazily in-body; no z3 / tree_sitter import at module scope).
produce_semantic_signals(finding, source_code, language=None) -> list[dict] is the sole public entry point.

An execution-sink violation (rule in {os_system, process_exec, subprocess_no_check}) corroborating an exec-class finding (category/cwe containing command_injection / CWE-78 / eval / CWE-95) yields {'tool':'ast_verifier','kind':'taint_flow','result':'proof','rule':...}; other ERROR-severity violations yield {'result':'match'} structural signals; clean source yields [].
Pure/deterministic: no network, clock, randomness, or subprocess; never raises on malformed/empty/non-str input (returns []).
No modification to ngv2/ast_verifier.py, ngv2/treesitter_verifier.py, ngv2/grounding_confidence_gate.py, or ngv2/session_gate.py; exactly one new file is added.

spec.objective: Build a new validation module ngv2/semantic_signals.py that wires the orphaned structural verifiers (ngv2.ast_verifier.ASTVerifier / ngv2.treesitter_verifier.TreeSitterVerifier) onto the live hunt path, converting their Violation objects into the {tool, kind, result} signal dicts that ngv2.grounding_confidence_gate.compute_confidence consumes.
functional_requirements: Emit ngv2/semantic_signals.py with EXACTLY the content given in the brief Deliverables block (verbatim docstring, constants, helpers, and produce_semantic_signals body).
Expose produce_semantic_signals(finding: dict, source_code: str, language: Optional[str]=None) -> list[dict] as the public interface.

Import ASTVerifier/SEVERITY_ERROR and TreeSitterVerifier lazily inside the function body so the module stays importable when tree-sitter grammar wheels (or z3) are absent; no z3/tree_sitter import at module scope.
Run TreeSitterVerifier().verify(source_code, lang) first, falling back to ASTVerifier().verify(source_code) on exception, and return [] if both fail or the lazy import fails.

Convert an execution-sink violation (rule in _EXEC_RULES={os_system,process_exec,subprocess_no_check}) that corroborates an exec-class finding (category/id/cwe blob containing command_injection/CWE-78/eval/CWE-95, case-insensitive) into a structural-proof signal {'tool':'ast_verifier','kind':'taint_flow','result':'proof','rule':rule}.

Convert other ERROR-severity violations into {'tool':'ast_verifier','kind':'structural','result':'match','rule':rule}; skip rule=='tree_sitter_unavailable'; clean source yields no signal; sort proof signals first then by rule.

Be pure/deterministic (no network/clock/randomness/subprocess) and never raise on malformed input: non-str or blank source_code returns []; language is inferred from the evidence path suffix (.py->python, .js/.jsx/.ts/.tsx->javascript, .c/.h->c, .java->java) defaulting to python.
spec.interfaces: produce_semantic_signals(finding: dict, source_code: str, language: str | None = None) -> list[dict]; helpers _language_for(finding)->str and _is_exec_finding(finding)->bool; module-level constants _EXEC_RULES (frozenset) and _EXEC_FINDING (tuple).
edge_cases: source_code is None / non-str / empty / whitespace-only -> return [].
Lazy import of verifier classes raises (tree-sitter/z3 wheels absent) -> return [].
TreeSitterVerifier.verify raises -> fall back to ASTVerifier.verify; if that also raises -> return [].
result has no .violations attribute or violations is None -> treated as empty list.
Violation with rule=='tree_sitter_unavailable' is skipped (no signal).
Exec-sink rule present but finding is NOT exec-class -> emit only a {'result':'match'} structural signal if severity is ERROR, never a proof.
finding lacking category/cwe/evidence/file fields -> _is_exec_finding and _language_for degrade gracefully (default python, non-exec).
non_goals: Do NOT modify ngv2/ast_verifier.py, ngv2/treesitter_verifier.py, ngv2/grounding_confidence_gate.py, or ngv2/session_gate.py.
Do NOT call the network, a subprocess, a clock, or an LLM; no randomness.
Do NOT import z3 or tree_sitter at module scope (lazy in-body only).
Do NOT touch any module other than the single new file ngv2/semantic_signals.py.
spec.implementation_notes:
Paste the Deliverables file verbatim. The signal dict shape must match what compute_confidence consumes: kind in {'taint_flow','formal_path','live_poc'} with result=='proof' is treated as a structural proof driving CONFIRMED. SEVERITY_ERROR=='ERROR' in ngv2.ast_verifier. The 'rule' key is carried for determinism/debuggability and to enable the stable sort (proof-first, then rule).

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Inline Python source strings: one with a real os.system(...) sink, one clean; finding dicts like {'id':'command_injection','category':'command_injection','cwe':'CWE-78','evidence':['svc.py:3']} (exec-class) and a non-exec finding; malformed findings (missing fields); non-str/empty source. All hermetic via the real stdlib AST verifier — no network/subprocess.

token_budget_ratio.note: Implementation is a verbatim paste of the Deliverables file; the bulk of effort/tokens belongs to the oracle and supporting assertions.
